name: Pro-Innovation Bias
description: People or organizations can overvalue novelty, assuming a new technology, feature, or process is good mainly because it is innovative. The bias shows up when limits, harms, maintenance cost, or user fit are underweighted in the excitement of the new.
design_relevance_note: Directly relevant to AI features, automation rollouts, redesigns, and '0-to-1' roadmap bets: teams can overpromote the innovation itself while under-testing whether it solves the right problem or introduces new user harm.
myth_risk_note: Pro-innovation bias, as documented in the available literature, is a research/methodological bias -- scholars disproportionately study and publish successful innovations -- not a validated individual cognitive bias. No direct empirical evidence was found for a cognitive bias where individuals systematically overvalue innovations in their own personal decision-making.
prevalence_note: Used regularly in critical design, responsible-AI, civic-tech, and STS-adjacent conversations, but far less often in mainstream product-design or CRO-style bias checklists.
